subject: Rebalance: Dedicated capacity reallocation request (Cobalt launch vs Nimbus expansion)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rebalance: Dedicated capacity reallocation request (Cobalt launch vs Nimbus expansion)

Team —

We have an urgent contention between two committed deals for Q2: CobaltAI (RDW-DA-2028-0819) is targeting a soft launch on 4/8 and their production profile needs ~120 concurrent RTX-6000-equivalent GPUs for initial traffic. Nimbus (internal strategic pilot) is accelerating a model migration and expects a temporary 40-GPU spike over the same window.

Current standing: we only have ~200 dedicated GPUs in the us-west reserved pool that are compatible with both workloads without degrading SLOs. With both going full, we oversubscribe by ~40 GPUs.

Options on the table (high level):
- Honor both commitments by procuring short-term burst capacity (costly, ~6k/day)
- Temporarily reassign 40 GPUs from Nimbus to Cobalt and provide Nimbus with burst/backfill on older A100 tranche
- Negotiate delayed start with Cobalt (unpopular; they are contractually sensitive)

I attached a capacity_impact_grid.xlsx and a proposed_rebalancing.pdf with quick numbers. Need an internal decision and an action owner by EOD tomorrow so we can update Sales/CS and notify Cobalt.

Ask: please respond with a recommended approach and whether there are technical blockers for moving 40 GPUs between dedicated tranches. If you have a lower-cost split (e.g., 20 GPU reassign + 20 burst credits) that preserves both deals, state it.

Marcus
Director, Dedicated Capacity Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rebalance: Dedicated capacity reallocation request (Cobalt launch vs Nimbus expansion)

Marcus —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick reaction and proposal:

1) Prioritize contractual commitments: Cobalt has a signed reserved capacity addendum for the April window. Our playbook should bias to keep their baseline intact.

2) Short-term compromise: move 20 GPUs from Nimbus to Cobalt immediately; offer Nimbus 20 GPUs of night-time preemptible capacity plus 4 weeks of burst credits (they're internal, we can flex). This reduces the immediate delta to +0 (they still get their core launch figures) and buys time.

3) Cost trade: burst capacity for 20 GPUs for two weeks (~$14k) vs; procurement of a short-term rented tranche (~$42k). Suggest the cheaper mix and monitor.

4) Action owners: Ops (Karthik) to confirm compatibility/migration friction; Account (Monica) to communicate revised timeline to Nimbus stakeholders; Sales (Marcus) to confirm with Cobalt that 20 GPU uplift is acceptable.

If Ops flags that we cannot safely carve 20 GPUs from Nimbus without violating their migration SLO, we fallback to the procurement option and ask Finance for emergency approval.

-Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_rebalancing.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Rebalance: Dedicated capacity reallocation request (Cobalt launch vs Nimbus expansion)

Folks —

Technical constraints and realistic options from Ops:

- We can reassign GPUs between tranches, but moving full production images and KV caches for larger models takes time and has an availability impact during cutover (expected 4–6 hours per tranche).
- We can increase packing efficiency (model quantization + contiguous allocation) and reclaim ~6–8 GPUs within 48 hours, but that requires coordination with Release Engineering on a hotfix window.
- Older A100 tranche is compatible with Nimbus workload (slower latency but within their non-real-time SLO). Moving 20 GPUs there is low-friction, 1–2 hour cutover.

Recommendation (practical):
1) Immediately carve 20 GPUs from Nimbus and place them into Cobalt's tranche for the launch window. Ops will perform a 1–2 hour cutover tonight during the low-traffic maintenance window.
2) Simultaneously run an efficiency reclaim play (packing/quant) to salvage additional 6 GPUs in 48 hours.
3) If Cobalt still needs more after these two steps, approve short-term rented burst for up to 14 days for the remaining delta (costed in Marcus's note).

I will create an INF ticket and schedule the cutover tonight. Need explicit sign-off from Sales (Marcus) to commit to the 20-GPU carve and from Marissa on the credit/comp package for Nimbus.

-Karthik
VP, Infrastructure Operations
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Decision: temporary rebalancing for Cobalt launch (RDW-DA-2028-0819)

Team —

Decision and actions based on the thread and Ops analysis:

Decision:
- Approve temporary rebalancing: move 20 GPUs from Nimbus to Cobalt immediately (cutover tonight).
- Run packing/quant reclaim play to recover +6 GPUs within 48 hours.
- Hold back an emergency rented-burst option as contingency (Finance on standby).

Commercial mitigations:
- Provide Nimbus with 4 weeks of burst credits equivalent to 20 GPUs and priority scheduling for their next maintenance window.
- Offer Cobalt a one-time launch support credit (5% of first-month committed spend) to smooth the relationship.

Action items and owners:
- Karthik: create INF-4821, schedule cutover (ETA: tonight low-traffic window), confirm KV cache migration checklist.
- Marissa: draft customer note to Nimbus and confirm credit mechanics (CC Finance).
- Monica: notify Cobalt legal/ops of the 20-GPU uplift and the formal fallback policy; copy in Caroline.
- Marcus: follow up with Finance on rented-burst approval and keep Execs updated if we hit any further shortfall.

Monitoring and rollback:
- Ops to monitor utilization metric streams and latency SLO in real-time; if tail latency exceeds 1.5x baseline for >15 minutes, trigger immediate rollback to prior allocation.

I'll update HubSpot and create the JIRA link below. If there are no objections within 2 hours I will execute the cutover.

Marcus
